newsitem.title: USA: U.S. stocks hold gains at midday, await earnings.
newsitem.headline: U.S. stocks hold gains at midday, await earnings.

text.p: U.S. stocks were firmly higher at midday Tuesday, recovering from yesterday's late-session declines amid a strengthening technology sector and optimism for the upcoming earnings reporting period.
The Dow Jones Industrial Average was up 51 points, or 0.66 percent, at 7910. A strong early rise in the index prompted the New York Stock Exchange to set curbs on index-arbitrage trading.
The Nasdaq composite, laden with technology stocks, gained around seven points, or 0.49 percent, to 1478.
"The market is coming back from yesterday's late session sell-off, which is appropriate," said Paul Rich, a trader at BT Brokerage. "Technology stocks are strong, which is driving the market up."
On Monday, strength in large-capitalization technology stocks pushed Nasdaq to another record high.
The same stocks made further gains in brisk trade today. Intel Corp rose 7/8 to 146-1/4, Microsoft Corp gained 1-3/8 to 130-7/8, and Compaq Computer Corp was up 4-3/4 to 119-1/4.
"The overall market is hopeful second quarter earnings will be good, though the proof is in the pudding, of course," said Sam Stovall, an analyst at S&P Industry Reports.
Among key earnings, Motorola Inc and Advanced Micro Devices Inc are to report second quarter results after the market close today.
Motorola's earnings are expected to be up slightly from the first quarter's $0.53 per share and the year-earlier $0.54 per share, analysts said.
The First Call consensus earnings estimate for Motorola is $0.56 per share.
